stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether guided hints help children learn to solve puzzles. They recruited 64 five-year-old children and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition solved practice puzzles with hints from an adult that were gradually reduced. Children in the other condition solved the same practice puzzles alone. The researchers then recorded the number of new puzzles out of ten that each child later solved without help.

Researchers collected data from 1,200 teenagers. For each one, they recorded the number of hours of social media use per day and score on a depression questionnaire. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.28.

Researchers investigated whether practice quizzes improve memory more than rereading. They recruited 120 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition read a passage once and then took three practice quizzes on it. Participants in the other condition read the same passage four times. The researchers then recorded the percentage of questions that each participant answered correctly on a test one week later.

Researchers investigated whether a night without sleep slows reaction time. They recruited 60 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition stayed awake all night in the laboratory. Participants in the other condition slept for eight hours in the laboratory. The researchers then recorded the average time in milliseconds that each participant took to press a button when a light appeared. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.41.

rows.group: The group that stayed awake all night
The group that slept for eight hours

stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether a phone conversation reduces what drivers notice. They recruited 64 licensed drivers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition held a hands-free phone conversation while using a driving simulator. Participants in the other condition used the driving simulator without a phone. The researchers then recorded the number of road signs out of 30 that each participant failed to notice.

Researchers collected data from 1,000 students. For each one, they recorded intelligence test score at age 11 and average school grade at age 16. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.60.

Researchers investigated whether children imitate aggressive behavior that they observe. They recruited 72 preschool children and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition watched a video of an adult hitting an inflatable doll. Children in the other condition watched a video of an adult playing quietly with other toys. The researchers then recorded the number of times that each child hit the doll during ten minutes of free play.

Researchers investigated whether the wording of a question changes what witnesses remember. They recruited 100 adult volunteers who watched a film of a car accident and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition were asked how fast the cars were going when they smashed into each other. Participants in the other condition were asked how fast the cars were going when they contacted each other. The researchers then recorded the speed in kilometers per hour that each participant wrote down.

Researchers investigated whether the color of a drink affects the ability to identify its flavor. They recruited 70 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition tasted ten fruit drinks whose colors did not match their flavors. Participants in the other condition tasted the same ten drinks with matching colors. The researchers then recorded the number of flavors out of ten that each participant named correctly.

Researchers collected data from 350 adults. For each one, they recorded the number of stressful life events in the past year and the number of colds in the past year. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.33.

Researchers investigated whether keeping a gratitude journal raises well-being. They recruited 110 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition wrote down three things they were grateful for every night for a month. Participants in the other condition wrote down three things they had done every night for a month. The researchers then recorded each participant's rating of life satisfaction on a scale from 1 to 10 at the end of the month.
Researchers collected data from 450 adults. For each one, they recorded optimism score and the number of days of illness in a year. The correlation between the two measures was r = −0.30.

Researchers investigated whether an expected reward reduces children's later interest in drawing. They recruited 60 preschool children who enjoyed drawing and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition were promised a certificate for drawing and received it. Children in the other condition drew with no reward mentioned. The researchers then recorded the number of minutes that each child chose to spend drawing during free time one week later.
Researchers collected data from 300 fifth-grade students. For each one, they recorded working memory span and reading comprehension score. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.52.

Researchers investigated whether regular aerobic exercise improves memory in older adults. They recruited 100 adults aged 60 to 75 and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition walked briskly for 40 minutes three times a week for six months. Participants in the other condition did gentle stretching for the same amount of time. The researchers then recorded the number of locations that each participant correctly recalled on a spatial memory test.

Researchers investigated whether a smiling expression makes cartoons seem funnier. They recruited 90 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition held a pen between their teeth, which produces a smile. Participants in the other condition held a pen between their lips, which prevents a smile. The researchers then recorded the rating from 1 to 10 that each participant gave to a set of cartoons.

Read the summary of a hypothetical study, then answer parts A to F.

**Introduction.** Researchers investigated whether guided hints help children learn to solve puzzles. They hypothesized that help from an adult would affect problem-solving skill.

**Participants.** The sample was 64 five-year-old children, recruited from one city. Parents gave informed consent, each child gave assent, and the plan was approved by an institutional review board. Families could withdraw at any time.

**Method.** The children were randomly assigned to one of two conditions. Children in one condition solved practice puzzles with hints from an adult that were gradually reduced. Children in the other condition solved the same practice puzzles alone. The researchers recorded the number of new puzzles out of ten that each child later solved without help.

**Results.** The group that received hints: mean new puzzles solved (out of 10) = 7.2. The group that practiced alone: mean new puzzles solved (out of 10) = 4.6. The difference was statistically significant (p = 0.01).

Use the three hypothetical sources to answer the question: **How does long-term stress affect health, and what reduces its effects?**

**Source A.** In a study of 350 adults, the number of stressful life events in the past year correlated with the number of colds in that year (r = +0.33). Adults who reported sleeping less tended to report both more stress and more colds.

**Source B.** In an experiment, 84 office workers were randomly assigned to practice mindfulness meditation or to listen to an audiobook for twenty minutes a day. After eight weeks, the meditation group had a mean cortisol level of 9.8 nmol/L and the audiobook group 13.5 nmol/L (p = 0.02).

**Source C.** Researchers followed 500 people for a year after a major flood. Those who reported strong support from family and friends had fewer symptoms of illness and depression than those who reported little support.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the identity status of a person who is actively exploring options but has not yet made a commitment?

options.why: Identity foreclosure is the identity status of a person who has made a commitment without exploring options.
Identity diffusion is the identity status of a person who has neither explored options nor made a commitment.
Correct. Identity moratorium is the identity status of a person who is actively exploring options but has not yet made a commitment.
Identity achievement is the identity status of a person who has explored options and made a commitment.

questions.explanation: Identity moratorium is the identity status of a person who is actively exploring options but has not yet made a commitment.

questions.stem: What is the independent variable in this study?

options.text: The number of participants in the study
options.why: This is the sample size, not a variable the researchers changed.
Correct. The independent variable is the factor the researchers changed between the two conditions.
This was measured, not manipulated: it is the dependent variable.
This is a procedure for forming the groups, not a variable.

questions.explanation: The independent variable is the factor the researchers changed between the two conditions.

questions.stem: In a group project with one shared grade, each of the five members does less work than they would on an individual project. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Deindividuation is the loss of self-awareness and self-restraint in group situations that provide arousal and anonymity.
Social facilitation is the improved performance on simple or well-learned tasks in the presence of others.
Groupthink is the kind of thinking in which the desire for agreement in a group overrides a realistic evaluation of alternatives.
Correct. Social loafing is the tendency for people to put in less effort when working in a group than when working alone.

questions.explanation: Social loafing is the tendency for people to put in less effort when working in a group than when working alone.

questions.stem: A tree partly covers a house in a painting, so viewers see the tree as closer. Which depth cue is this?

options.why: Correct. Interposition is the monocular depth cue in which an object that partly blocks another is seen as closer.
Convergence is the binocular depth cue based on how far the eyes turn inward to focus on a near object.
Relative size is the monocular depth cue in which the object that casts the smaller image is seen as farther away.
Linear perspective is the monocular depth cue in which parallel lines seem to meet in the distance.

questions.explanation: Interposition is the monocular depth cue in which an object that partly blocks another is seen as closer.

questions.stem: English speakers say 'white house' while Spanish speakers say 'casa blanca', with the adjective second. This difference is one of which of the following?

options.why: Semantics is the rules by which we get meaning from words and sentences.
A morpheme is the smallest unit of language that carries meaning.
A phoneme is the smallest distinctive unit of sound in a language.
Correct. Syntax is the rules for ordering words into sentences.

questions.explanation: Syntax is the rules for ordering words into sentences.

questions.stem: When a dog lunges at him, Evan's heart pounds and his muscles tense, ready for him to run or defend himself. Which response to stress is this?

options.why: The tend-and-befriend response is the response to stress of caring for others and seeking social support.
A stressor is an event or situation that a person sees as threatening or challenging.
Correct. The fight-or-flight response is the response to stress in which the sympathetic nervous system prepares the body to attack or escape.
Eustress is the positive, motivating stress that comes from a challenge.

questions.explanation: The fight-or-flight response is the response to stress in which the sympathetic nervous system prepares the body to attack or escape.

questions.stem: A drug sits in the receptors for a neurotransmitter and prevents the neurotransmitter from having any effect. The drug is acting as which of the following?

options.why: Tolerance is the need for larger doses of a drug to get the same effect after repeated use.
An agonist is a drug that increases the action of a neurotransmitter, for example by mimicking it.
Correct. An antagonist is a drug that decreases the action of a neurotransmitter, for example by blocking its receptors.
A reuptake inhibitor is a drug that keeps a neurotransmitter in the synapse longer by blocking its reabsorption.

questions.explanation: An antagonist is a drug that decreases the action of a neurotransmitter, for example by blocking its receptors.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the view that disorders result from learned associations and reinforcement?

options.why: The cognitive perspective is the view that disorders result from distorted or irrational ways of thinking.
The biological perspective is the view that disorders result from genetic, brain or chemical causes.
Correct. The behavioral perspective is the view that disorders result from learned associations and reinforcement.
The sociocultural perspective is the view that disorders result from social and cultural factors, such as poverty and discrimination.

questions.explanation: The behavioral perspective is the view that disorders result from learned associations and reinforcement.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the structure that regulates hunger, thirst, body temperature and sexual behavior and controls the pituitary gland?

options.why: The hippocampus is the structure that forms new explicit memories of facts and events.
The cerebral cortex is the wrinkled outer layer of the brain, which handles thinking, perception and voluntary movement.
Correct. The hypothalamus is the structure that regulates hunger, thirst, body temperature and sexual behavior and controls the pituitary gland.
The corpus callosum is the band of fibers that connects the two hemispheres of the brain.

questions.explanation: The hypothalamus is the structure that regulates hunger, thirst, body temperature and sexual behavior and controls the pituitary gland.

questions.stem: A coil held against a patient's scalp sends magnetic pulses into the cortex to relieve depression, with no anesthesia and no seizure. Which treatment is this?

options.why: A lobotomy is the now-abandoned form of psychosurgery that cut the nerves connecting the frontal lobes to the rest of the brain.
Electroconvulsive therapy is the treatment for severe depression in which a brief electric current is passed through the brain of an anesthetized patient.
Correct. Transcranial magnetic stimulation is the treatment in which repeated magnetic pulses are applied to the surface of the brain to treat depression.
Psychotropic medication is any drug that acts on the brain to treat the symptoms of a psychological disorder.

questions.explanation: Transcranial magnetic stimulation is the treatment in which repeated magnetic pulses are applied to the surface of the brain to treat depression.

questions.stem: Lena is so terrified of spiders that she will not enter any room where she has ever seen one. Which disorder does this suggest?

options.why: Agoraphobia is the disorder in which a person fears and avoids public places from which escape might be difficult.
Correct. A specific phobia is the disorder in which a person has an intense, irrational fear of a particular object or situation.
Ataque de nervios is the culture-bound anxiety syndrome, found mainly among people of Caribbean descent, marked by shouting, crying and a feeling of being out of control.
Panic disorder is the disorder in which a person has repeated, unexpected episodes of intense fear with physical symptoms such as chest pain.

questions.explanation: A specific phobia is the disorder in which a person has an intense, irrational fear of a particular object or situation.

questions.stem: Students are asked whether each word on a list rhymes with 'cat'. Which level of processing does this task use?

options.why: Correct. Phonemic encoding is the encoding of a word based on its sound.
Semantic encoding is the deep encoding of a word based on its meaning.
Effortful processing is the encoding that requires attention and conscious effort.
Implicit memory is the memory of skills and learned associations that is retained without conscious recall.

questions.explanation: Phonemic encoding is the encoding of a word based on its sound.

questions.stem: Why is this study not an experiment?

options.why: Experiments also use numerical data.
Sample size does not determine the research method.

options.text: The researchers did not manipulate a variable or randomly assign anyone to conditions
options.why: Correct. An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.
Experiments also test hypotheses.

questions.explanation: An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes applied behavior analysis?

options.text: The behavioral treatment that pairs an unwanted behavior with an unpleasant stimulus
options.why: That describes aversion therapy.

options.text: The technique of using electronic monitoring to show a person their body's signals so that they can learn to control them
options.why: That describes biofeedback.

options.text: The use of the principles of conditioning to increase helpful behaviors and reduce harmful ones
options.why: Correct. This is what applied behavior analysis means.

options.text: The behavioral system in which people earn tokens for desired behavior and exchange them for rewards
options.why: That describes a token economy.

questions.explanation: Applied behavior analysis is the use of the principles of conditioning to increase helpful behaviors and reduce harmful ones.

questions.stem: Lee assumes that all teenagers are careless drivers. This belief is an example of which of the following?

options.why: An implicit attitude is an attitude that a person holds without being aware of it.
Correct. A stereotype is a generalized belief about a group of people.
Discrimination is unjustified negative behavior toward a group and its members.
Prejudice is an unjustified negative attitude toward a group and its members.

questions.explanation: A stereotype is a generalized belief about a group of people.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes integrity versus despair?

options.text: Erikson's stage in middle adulthood, in which people seek to contribute to the world through family and work
options.why: That describes generativity versus stagnation.

options.text: Erikson's stage in young adulthood, in which people seek close, lasting relationships
options.why: That describes intimacy versus isolation.

options.text: Erikson's stage in adolescence, in which teenagers work out who they are
options.why: That describes identity versus role confusion.

options.text: Erikson's stage in late adulthood, in which people look back on life with satisfaction or regret
options.why: Correct. This is what integrity versus despair means.

questions.explanation: Integrity versus despair is Erikson's stage in late adulthood, in which people look back on life with satisfaction or regret.

questions.stem: Neither the participants nor the assistants who recorded the results knew which condition each participant was in. What is this procedure called?

options.why: In a single-blind procedure only the participants are unaware.
Correct. Keeping both participants and researchers unaware of the conditions reduces bias from expectations.
That is a therapy technique, not a research control.
Random sampling is how participants are chosen from a population.

questions.explanation: Keeping both participants and researchers unaware of the conditions reduces bias from expectations.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the Yerkes-Dodson law?

options.text: The theory that people are motivated to keep an ideal level of alertness and stimulation
options.why: That describes arousal theory.

options.text: The theory that behavior is driven by fixed, inborn patterns that are not learned
options.why: That describes instinct theory.

options.text: The principle that performance is best at a moderate level of arousal
options.why: Correct. This is what the Yerkes-Dodson law means.

options.text: The theory that a physical need creates a state of tension that motivates behavior to reduce it
options.why: That describes drive-reduction theory.

questions.explanation: The Yerkes-Dodson law is the principle that performance is best at a moderate level of arousal.

questions.stem: Ed feels strong resentment toward his sister but treats her with exaggerated kindness and praise. Which defense mechanism is this?

options.why: Correct. Reaction formation is the defense mechanism of acting in the opposite way to one's unacceptable impulses.
Regression is the defense mechanism of retreating to behavior from an earlier stage of development.
Sublimation is the defense mechanism of turning unacceptable impulses into socially valued activities.
Repression is the defense mechanism of pushing anxiety-arousing thoughts and memories out of awareness.

questions.explanation: Reaction formation is the defense mechanism of acting in the opposite way to one's unacceptable impulses.

questions.stem: A researcher claims that dreams have no hidden meaning; the cortex simply builds a story out of random signals from the brainstem. Which theory is this?

options.why: Restoration is the repair of body and brain tissue that takes place during sleep.
The consolidation theory is the theory that dreaming helps sort and strengthen the day's memories.
Memory consolidation is the strengthening of memories that takes place during sleep.
Correct. The activation-synthesis theory is the theory that dreams are the brain's attempt to make sense of random neural activity during sleep.

questions.explanation: The activation-synthesis theory is the theory that dreams are the brain's attempt to make sense of random neural activity during sleep.

questions.stem: A dog salivates to a high tone that signals food but not to a low tone that never does. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Extinction is the weakening of a conditioned response when the conditioned stimulus is repeatedly presented alone.
Spontaneous recovery is the reappearance of a weakened conditioned response after a rest period.
Higher-order conditioning is the pairing of a new neutral stimulus with an existing conditioned stimulus to create a second conditioned stimulus.
Correct. Stimulus discrimination is the learned ability to respond to the conditioned stimulus but not to similar stimuli.

questions.explanation: Stimulus discrimination is the learned ability to respond to the conditioned stimulus but not to similar stimuli.

questions.stem: On a dark night, Kai can make out shapes but not colors. Which receptor cells is he relying on?

options.why: The blind spot is the point where the optic nerve leaves the eye, which has no receptor cells.
The retina is the light-sensitive inner surface at the back of the eye that contains the receptor cells.
Correct. Rods is the receptor cells that detect black, white and gray and work in dim light and peripheral vision.
The lens is the transparent structure that changes shape to focus light on the retina.

questions.explanation: Rods is the receptor cells that detect black, white and gray and work in dim light and peripheral vision.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant
options.why: A p value of 0.41 is far above 0.05.

options.text: The study shows that the two conditions always give identical results
options.why: A non-significant result does not show that there is no effect at all.

options.text: The difference between the groups is not statistically significant, so it could easily be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

options.text: The independent variable had a large effect
options.why: The averages are close and the difference is not significant.

questions.explanation: A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: For three years, Otto has felt low and tired on most days, though he still manages to work. Which disorder does this suggest?

options.why: Bipolar I disorder is the disorder in which a person has full manic episodes, usually alternating with depression.
Correct. Persistent depressive disorder is the disorder in which a person has a mildly depressed mood on most days for at least two years.
Bipolar II disorder is the disorder in which a person alternates between depression and a milder form of mania called hypomania.
Mania is a state of extreme energy, overconfidence, racing thoughts and little need for sleep.

questions.explanation: Persistent depressive disorder is the disorder in which a person has a mildly depressed mood on most days for at least two years.

questions.stem: Although he is bright and works hard, ten-year-old Theo reads far below the level expected for his age. Which disorder does this suggest?

options.why: Anorexia nervosa is the eating disorder in which a person restricts food to the point of being dangerously underweight, with an intense fear of gaining weight.
Correct. A specific learning disorder is the neurodevelopmental disorder marked by persistent difficulty in reading, writing or math despite normal intelligence.
Binge-eating disorder is the eating disorder in which a person repeatedly eats very large amounts and feels distress, without purging afterward.
Bulimia nervosa is the eating disorder in which a person binges on food and then makes up for it by vomiting, fasting or excessive exercise.

questions.explanation: A specific learning disorder is the neurodevelopmental disorder marked by persistent difficulty in reading, writing or math despite normal intelligence.

questions.stem: Paranoid, schizoid and schizotypal personality disorders belong to which cluster?

options.why: Correct. Cluster A is the group of personality disorders marked by odd or eccentric behavior: paranoid, schizoid and schizotypal.
A personality disorder is a lasting, rigid pattern of behavior and inner experience that differs from cultural expectations and impairs functioning.
Cluster C is the group of personality disorders marked by anxious or fearful behavior: avoidant, dependent and obsessive-compulsive.
Cluster B is the group of personality disorders marked by dramatic, emotional or erratic behavior: antisocial, borderline, histrionic and narcissistic.

questions.explanation: Cluster A is the group of personality disorders marked by odd or eccentric behavior: paranoid, schizoid and schizotypal.

questions.stem: Selye found that animals under prolonged stress passed through alarm, then resistance, then exhaustion. What is this three-phase pattern called?

options.why: Correct. The general adaptation syndrome is Selye's three-phase description of the body's response to long-term stress: alarm, resistance and exhaustion.
The resistance phase is the second phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the body stays highly aroused to cope with a continuing stressor.
The exhaustion phase is the third phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the body's resources run out and illness becomes more likely.
The alarm reaction is the first phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the sympathetic nervous system is suddenly activated.

questions.explanation: The general adaptation syndrome is Selye's three-phase description of the body's response to long-term stress: alarm, resistance and exhaustion.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes an avoidance-avoidance conflict?

options.text: The desire to do something to gain a reward or avoid a punishment
options.why: That describes extrinsic motivation.

options.text: A conflict in which a person must choose between two attractive options
options.why: That describes an approach-approach conflict.

options.text: A conflict in which a person must choose between two unattractive options
options.why: Correct. This is what an avoidance-avoidance conflict means.

options.text: The desire to do something for its own sake, because it is enjoyable or satisfying
options.why: That describes intrinsic motivation.

questions.explanation: An avoidance-avoidance conflict is a conflict in which a person must choose between two unattractive options.

questions.stem: Which group served as the control group?

options.text: The group that drove without a phone
options.why: Correct. The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.

options.text: Neither group, because the study had no comparison condition
options.why: The second condition is the comparison.
Only the comparison group is the control group.

options.text: The group that talked on the phone
options.why: This group received the treatment being tested: it is the experimental group.

questions.explanation: The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.

questions.stem: A therapist stops using a technique when she sees that it is making her client worse. Which ethical principle is she following?

options.why: Fidelity is the ethical principle that psychologists must be trustworthy and keep their professional promises.
Correct. Nonmaleficence is the ethical principle that psychologists must avoid doing harm.
Integrity is the ethical principle that psychologists must be honest and accurate.

options.text: Respect for people's rights and dignity
options.why: Respect for people's rights and dignity is the ethical principle that psychologists must protect privacy, confidentiality and the right of people to make their own choices.

questions.explanation: Nonmaleficence is the ethical principle that psychologists must avoid doing harm.

questions.stem: A second laboratory repeats a famous memory study with new participants to check the result. This is an example of which of the following?

options.why: An experiment is the research method in which a researcher manipulates a variable and randomly assigns participants, which allows conclusions about cause and effect.
Falsifiability is the quality of a claim that it could be shown to be wrong by evidence.
A survey is the research method of collecting self-reported attitudes or behaviors from a sample by asking questions.
Correct. Replication is the repeating of a study with different participants to see whether the finding holds.

questions.explanation: Replication is the repeating of a study with different participants to see whether the finding holds.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes short-term memory?

options.text: The sensory memory of a sound, which lasts three or four seconds
options.why: That describes echoic memory.

options.text: The memory store that briefly holds a few items, about seven, before they are stored or forgotten
options.why: Correct. This is what short-term memory means.

options.text: The active processing of information held in mind, combining new input with knowledge from long-term memory
options.why: That describes working memory.

options.text: The brief sensory memory of a visual image, which lasts a few tenths of a second
options.why: That describes iconic memory.

questions.explanation: Short-term memory is the memory store that briefly holds a few items, about seven, before they are stored or forgotten.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as in classical conditioning, the originally neutral stimulus that triggers a response after being paired with another stimulus?

options.why: Correct. The conditioned stimulus is in classical conditioning, the originally neutral stimulus that triggers a response after being paired with another stimulus.
The unconditioned response is in classical conditioning, the natural, unlearned response to a stimulus.
The unconditioned stimulus is in classical conditioning, the stimulus that triggers a response naturally, without learning.
The conditioned response is in classical conditioning, the learned response to a previously neutral stimulus.

questions.explanation: The conditioned stimulus is in classical conditioning, the originally neutral stimulus that triggers a response after being paired with another stimulus.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes melatonin?

options.text: The hormone released by fat cells that signals fullness and reduces hunger
options.why: That describes leptin.

options.text: The hormone released by an empty stomach that increases hunger
options.why: That describes ghrelin.

options.text: The hormone released by the pineal gland that makes a person sleepy
options.why: Correct. This is what melatonin means.

options.text: The hormone released by the adrenal glands that raises heart rate and energy during stress
options.why: That describes adrenaline.

questions.explanation: Melatonin is the hormone released by the pineal gland that makes a person sleepy.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a questionnaire with many true-false or agree-disagree items that measures a range of traits?

options.why: Self-concept is all the thoughts and feelings a person has in answer to the question 'Who am I?'.
Correct. A personality inventory is a questionnaire with many true-false or agree-disagree items that measures a range of traits.
Reciprocal determinism is the idea that a person's behavior, thoughts and environment all influence one another.
Self-esteem is a person's overall feeling of self-worth.

questions.explanation: A personality inventory is a questionnaire with many true-false or agree-disagree items that measures a range of traits.

questions.stem: To choose 500 students for a survey, a researcher uses a computer to pick names from the list of all students in the country. Which procedure is this?

options.why: Sampling bias is a flaw in selecting participants that makes the sample unlike the population.
Random assignment is the placing of participants in experimental conditions by chance.
A representative sample is a sample whose characteristics match those of the population it is drawn from.
Correct. Random sampling is the selecting of participants so that every member of the population has an equal chance of being chosen.

questions.explanation: Random sampling is the selecting of participants so that every member of the population has an equal chance of being chosen.

questions.stem: Why is this study not an experiment?

options.why: Experiments also use numerical data.
Experiments also test hypotheses.

options.text: The researchers did not manipulate a variable or randomly assign anyone to conditions
options.why: Correct. An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.
Sample size does not determine the research method.

questions.explanation: An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the mean?

options.text: A distribution with a few extremely low scores, which pull the mean below the median
options.why: That describes a negative skew.

options.text: A distribution with a few extremely high scores, which pull the mean above the median
options.why: That describes a positive skew.

options.text: The arithmetic average of a set of scores
options.why: Correct. This is what the mean means.

options.text: The difference between the highest and lowest scores
options.why: That describes the range.

questions.explanation: The mean is the arithmetic average of a set of scores.

questions.stem: Ebbinghaus found that most forgetting of nonsense syllables happened in the first hours, with little more lost over later weeks. What is this pattern called?

options.why: Correct. The forgetting curve is the pattern in which memory fades quickly at first and then levels off.
The tip-of-the-tongue phenomenon is the temporary inability to retrieve a word that one is sure one knows.
Proactive interference is the disruption of new learning by older memories.
Encoding failure is forgetting that happens because the information never entered long-term memory.

questions.explanation: The forgetting curve is the pattern in which memory fades quickly at first and then levels off.

questions.stem: What is the dependent variable in this study?

options.why: Correct. The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

options.text: The condition to which each one was assigned
options.why: This describes the independent variable.
A hypothesis is a prediction, not a variable.

options.text: The behavior of an adult model
options.why: This was manipulated by the researchers: it is the independent variable.

questions.explanation: The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

questions.stem: Each time Ed retells a childhood story, his brain rebuilds it, filling gaps with what probably happened. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Source amnesia is the inability to remember where, when or how a piece of information was learned.
The misinformation effect is the distortion of a memory by misleading information received after the event.
Imagination inflation is the increased confidence that an event happened after repeatedly imagining it.
Correct. Constructive memory is the building of a memory at retrieval from stored pieces, expectations and later information.

questions.explanation: Constructive memory is the building of a memory at retrieval from stored pieces, expectations and later information.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the tendency to remember the first items in a list well?

options.why: The serial position effect is the tendency to remember the first and last items in a list better than the middle ones.
The recency effect is the tendency to remember the last items in a list well.
Correct. The primacy effect is the tendency to remember the first items in a list well.
The spacing effect is the finding that study spread over time produces better long-term memory than study crammed together.

questions.explanation: The primacy effect is the tendency to remember the first items in a list well.

questions.stem: When two brothers fight over a game, their father removes the game, and the fighting decreases. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Positive reinforcement is the strengthening of a behavior by adding a pleasant stimulus after it.
Negative reinforcement is the strengthening of a behavior by removing an unpleasant stimulus after it.
Correct. Negative punishment is the weakening of a behavior by removing a pleasant stimulus after it.
Positive punishment is the weakening of a behavior by adding an unpleasant stimulus after it.

questions.explanation: Negative punishment is the weakening of a behavior by removing a pleasant stimulus after it.

questions.stem: Carl avoided fish after becoming ill only once. Learning that takes place after a single pairing is called which of the following?

options.why: Correct. One-trial conditioning is learning that happens after a single pairing of two stimuli.
Counterconditioning is the replacing of an unwanted response to a stimulus with a new response, by pairing the stimulus with something pleasant.
Biological preparedness is the inborn readiness to learn some associations, such as taste and nausea, more easily than others.
Habituation is the decrease in response to a stimulus that is presented over and over.

questions.explanation: One-trial conditioning is learning that happens after a single pairing of two stimuli.

questions.stem: Before taking part, each participant was told what the study would involve and what the risks were, and then agreed to take part. Which ethical guideline does this meet?

options.why: That is a research procedure, not an ethical guideline.
Debriefing happens after the study.
Correct. Participants must agree to take part after being told what the study involves.
Confidentiality is keeping participants' data private.

questions.explanation: Participants must agree to take part after being told what the study involves.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a person with more taste receptors than average, who experiences tastes more intensely?

options.why: A pheromone is a chemical signal released by one member of a species that affects the behavior of others.
Gustation is the sense of taste, which detects sweet, sour, salty, bitter, umami and oleogustus.
Correct. A supertaster is a person with more taste receptors than average, who experiences tastes more intensely.
Olfaction is the sense of smell, the only sense that does not pass through the thalamus first.

questions.explanation: A supertaster is a person with more taste receptors than average, who experiences tastes more intensely.

questions.stem: Years of loud concerts destroyed the hair cells in Dee's cochlea. Which kind of hearing loss does she have?

options.why: Place theory is the theory that we hear different pitches because different sound waves trigger different places on the cochlea's membrane.
Frequency theory is the theory that we hear pitch because the rate of nerve impulses matches the frequency of the sound.
Sound localization is the ability to tell where a sound comes from, using differences in timing and loudness between the two ears.
Correct. Sensorineural deafness is hearing loss caused by damage to the hair cells of the cochlea or to the auditory nerve.

questions.explanation: Sensorineural deafness is hearing loss caused by damage to the hair cells of the cochlea or to the auditory nerve.

questions.stem: Neither the participants nor the assistants who recorded the results knew which condition each participant was in. What is this procedure called?

options.why: Random sampling is how participants are chosen from a population.
In a single-blind procedure only the participants are unaware.
That is a therapy technique, not a research control.
Correct. Keeping both participants and researchers unaware of the conditions reduces bias from expectations.

questions.explanation: Keeping both participants and researchers unaware of the conditions reduces bias from expectations.

questions.stem: Why is this study not an experiment?

options.why: Sample size does not determine the research method.

options.text: The researchers did not manipulate a variable or randomly assign anyone to conditions
options.why: Correct. An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.
Experiments also use numerical data.
Experiments also test hypotheses.

questions.explanation: An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.

questions.stem: After failing every math test no matter how hard he studied, Finn stops studying altogether, saying nothing he does matters. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Instinctive drift is the tendency of a trained animal to return to its natural, inborn behaviors.
Correct. Learned helplessness is the passive giving up that follows repeated experiences of being unable to avoid bad events.
The law of effect is Thorndike's principle that behaviors followed by good outcomes become more likely and those followed by bad outcomes become less likely.
A secondary reinforcer is a reinforcer, such as money or praise, that gets its power through association with other rewards.

questions.explanation: Learned helplessness is the passive giving up that follows repeated experiences of being unable to avoid bad events.

questions.stem: A four-year-old invents a game and organizes her friends to play it. Which of Erikson's stages is this?

options.why: Trust versus mistrust is Erikson's stage in infancy, in which babies learn whether their needs will be met.
Industry versus inferiority is Erikson's stage in elementary school, in which children learn to feel competent or else feel inadequate.
Autonomy versus shame and doubt is Erikson's stage in toddlerhood, in which children learn to do things for themselves.
Correct. Initiative versus guilt is Erikson's stage in the preschool years, in which children learn to start tasks and carry out plans.

questions.explanation: Initiative versus guilt is Erikson's stage in the preschool years, in which children learn to start tasks and carry out plans.

questions.stem: Another research team repeats this study with new subjects and obtains the same result. What is this called?

options.why: That is explaining the study to participants afterward.
That is an in-depth study of one individual.
Correct. Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.
That is how subjects are placed in conditions.

questions.explanation: Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes an industrial-organizational psychologist?

options.text: A psychologist who studies behavior in the workplace to improve productivity and well-being
options.why: Correct. This is what an industrial-organizational psychologist means.

options.text: The tendency for a person to be less likely to help when other people are present
options.why: That describes the bystander effect.

options.text: The physical and emotional exhaustion that results from long-term stress at work
options.why: That describes burnout.

options.text: The expectation that people will help those who need help, even at a cost to themselves
options.why: That describes the social responsibility norm.

questions.explanation: An industrial-organizational psychologist is a psychologist who studies behavior in the workplace to improve productivity and well-being.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes social desirability bias?

options.text: The tendency to be more certain than correct about one's own judgments
options.why: That describes overconfidence.

options.text: The tendency of participants to answer in a way that makes them look good
options.why: Correct. This is what social desirability bias means.

options.text: The inaccuracy that arises when people describe their own behavior or feelings
options.why: That describes self-report bias.

options.text: The tendency, after learning an outcome, to believe one would have predicted it
options.why: That describes hindsight bias.

questions.explanation: Social desirability bias is the tendency of participants to answer in a way that makes them look good.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a fixed-ratio schedule?

options.text: The schedule in which the first response after an unpredictable amount of time is reinforced
options.why: That describes a variable-interval schedule.

options.text: The schedule in which the behavior is reinforced after an unpredictable number of responses
options.why: That describes a variable-ratio schedule.

options.text: The schedule in which the behavior is reinforced after a set number of responses
options.why: Correct. This is what a fixed-ratio schedule means.

options.text: The schedule in which the first response after a set amount of time is reinforced
options.why: That describes a fixed-interval schedule.

questions.explanation: A fixed-ratio schedule is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced after a set number of responses.

questions.stem: A clinician explains a patient's depression by her family history, her negative thinking style and her recent job loss together. Which model is this?

options.why: The diathesis-stress model is the view that a disorder develops when an inherited vulnerability is triggered by stressful experience.
Comorbidity is the presence of two or more disorders in the same person at the same time.
Correct. The biopsychosocial model is the view that disorders result from the interaction of biological, psychological and social factors.
An eclectic approach is the use of techniques from several types of therapy, depending on the client's problem.

questions.explanation: The biopsychosocial model is the view that disorders result from the interaction of biological, psychological and social factors.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes tardive dyskinesia?

options.text: A drug that reduces hallucinations and delusions by blocking dopamine receptors
options.why: That describes an antipsychotic drug.

options.text: A drug, such as an SSRI, that treats depression and anxiety by raising the availability of serotonin or norepinephrine
options.why: That describes an antidepressant.

options.text: A drug that reduces tension by depressing central nervous system activity and can be addictive
options.why: That describes an antianxiety drug.

options.text: The involuntary movements of the face and tongue that can result from long-term use of antipsychotic drugs
options.why: Correct. This is what tardive dyskinesia means.

questions.explanation: Tardive dyskinesia is the involuntary movements of the face and tongue that can result from long-term use of antipsychotic drugs.

questions.stem: Seven students took a memory test. Their scores were 14, 12, 11, 9, 11, 21, 6. What is the range of the scores?

options.why: That is the median.
That is the mean.
Correct. Subtract the lowest score from the highest.
That is the highest score.

questions.explanation: In order, the scores are 6, 9, 11, 11, 12, 14, 21. Subtract the lowest score from the highest. The one very high score pulls the mean (12) above the median (11), so the distribution is positively skewed.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the area in the left frontal lobe that controls speech production?

options.why: Hemispheric specialization is the tendency for each side of the brain to handle certain functions, such as language in the left hemisphere.
Contralateral control is the arrangement in which each hemisphere controls the opposite side of the body.
Wernicke's area is the area in the left temporal lobe that controls language comprehension.
Correct. Broca's area is the area in the left frontal lobe that controls speech production.

questions.explanation: Broca's area is the area in the left frontal lobe that controls speech production.

questions.stem: Sam is warm, quick to forgive and always willing to help. He would score high on which Big Five trait?

options.why: Extraversion is the Big Five trait of being sociable, outgoing and energetic.
Openness to experience is the Big Five trait of being imaginative, curious and willing to try new things.
Emotional stability is the Big Five trait of being calm and secure rather than anxious and moody.
Correct. Agreeableness is the Big Five trait of being kind, trusting and cooperative.

questions.explanation: Agreeableness is the Big Five trait of being kind, trusting and cooperative.

questions.stem: Neurotransmitters must cross a small space to reach the next neuron. What is this space called?

options.why: Correct. The synapse is the tiny gap between the sending neuron and the receiving neuron.
The cell body is the part of the neuron that contains the nucleus and keeps the cell alive.
The axon is the long fiber that carries the neural impulse away from the cell body toward other cells.
The axon terminals is the endings of the axon that release neurotransmitters.

questions.explanation: The synapse is the tiny gap between the sending neuron and the receiving neuron.

questions.stem: Why is this study not an experiment?

options.text: The researchers did not manipulate a variable or randomly assign anyone to conditions
options.why: Correct. An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.
Sample size does not determine the research method.
Experiments also use numerical data.
Experiments also test hypotheses.

questions.explanation: An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the frontal lobes?

options.text: The strip at the rear of the frontal lobes that controls voluntary movements
options.why: That describes the motor cortex.

options.text: The strip at the front of the parietal lobes that registers touch and body sensations
options.why: That describes the somatosensory cortex.

options.text: The lobes at the back of the head, which process visual information
options.why: That describes the occipital lobes.

options.text: The lobes behind the forehead, which handle planning, judgment and voluntary movement
options.why: Correct. This is what the frontal lobes means.

questions.explanation: The frontal lobes is the lobes behind the forehead, which handle planning, judgment and voluntary movement.

questions.stem: A child's parents and teachers meet regularly and work together. In ecological systems theory, this connection is part of which system?

options.why: The exosystem is in ecological systems theory, the settings that affect a child indirectly, such as a parent's workplace.
The chronosystem is in ecological systems theory, the life stage and historical events that affect a child.
The microsystem is in ecological systems theory, the groups that have direct contact with the child, such as family and school.
Correct. The mesosystem is in ecological systems theory, the relationships between the groups in a child's immediate surroundings.

questions.explanation: The mesosystem is in ecological systems theory, the relationships between the groups in a child's immediate surroundings.

questions.stem: Another research team repeats this study with new subjects and obtains the same result. What is this called?

options.why: That is an in-depth study of one individual.
That is explaining the study to participants afterward.
That is how subjects are placed in conditions.
Correct. Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.

questions.explanation: Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.

questions.stem: What does the correlation show?

options.text: The first measure causes the second
options.why: A correlation does not show cause and effect.

options.text: Higher values of the first measure tend to go with higher values of the second
options.why: Correct. A positive correlation means the two measures tend to move in the same direction.

options.text: Higher values of the first measure tend to go with lower values of the second
options.why: That would be a negative correlation.
A correlation of zero would show no relationship.

questions.explanation: A positive correlation means the two measures tend to move in the same direction.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the operational definition of the dependent variable?

options.why: This is the independent variable.

options.text: The number of locations that each participant correctly recalled on a spatial memory test
options.why: Correct. An operational definition states exactly how a variable is measured.

options.text: The random assignment of each one to a condition
options.why: This is a control procedure, not a definition of a variable.
This names the variable but does not say how it was measured.

questions.explanation: An operational definition states exactly how a variable is measured.

questions.stem: Two students have racing hearts before a speech; one labels the feeling as excitement and the other as fear. The difference in their emotions is due to which of the following?

options.why: Universal emotions is the basic emotions, such as happiness, sadness, fear and anger, whose facial expressions are recognized across cultures.
An elicitor is an event or stimulus that triggers an emotion.
The broaden-and-build theory is the theory that positive emotions widen a person's awareness and help build lasting skills and resources.
Correct. Cognitive appraisal is the interpretation of a situation, which shapes the emotion a person feels.

questions.explanation: Cognitive appraisal is the interpretation of a situation, which shapes the emotion a person feels.

questions.stem: A company gives applicants a test designed to predict how well they will learn computer programming. Which kind of test is this?

options.why: Correct. An aptitude test is a test that predicts a person's ability to learn or perform in the future.
Stereotype lift is the boost in performance that comes from awareness that another group is negatively stereotyped.
A growth mindset is the belief that intelligence can be developed through effort and learning.
An achievement test is a test that measures what a person has already learned.

questions.explanation: An aptitude test is a test that predicts a person's ability to learn or perform in the future.

questions.stem: After being shouted at by her boss, Gia goes home and shouts at her younger brother. Which defense mechanism is this?

options.why: Denial is the defense mechanism of refusing to accept a painful reality.
Projection is the defense mechanism of seeing one's own unacceptable impulses in other people.
Rationalization is the defense mechanism of giving a comfortable excuse in place of the real reason for a behavior.
Correct. Displacement is the defense mechanism of shifting an impulse from its real target to a safer one.

questions.explanation: Displacement is the defense mechanism of shifting an impulse from its real target to a safer one.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes an EEG?

options.text: A recording of the electrical waves that sweep across the brain's surface
options.why: Correct. This is what an EEG means.

options.text: An in-depth study of one individual, such as a patient with unusual brain damage
options.why: That describes a case study.

options.text: A scan that shows brain activity by tracking blood flow
options.why: That describes an fMRI.

options.text: The condition in which the two hemispheres cannot communicate because the corpus callosum has been cut
options.why: That describes a split brain.

questions.explanation: An EEG is a recording of the electrical waves that sweep across the brain's surface.

questions.stem: After losing a match, Eli thinks, 'I always fail at everything, and it is all my fault.' Which explanatory style is this?

options.why: The actor-observer bias is the tendency to explain our own behavior by the situation but other people's behavior by their traits.
The fundamental attribution error is the tendency, when judging other people's behavior, to overestimate personal traits and underestimate the situation.
Correct. A pessimistic explanatory style is the habit of explaining bad events as lasting, affecting everything and caused by oneself.
An optimistic explanatory style is the habit of explaining bad events as temporary, specific and caused by outside factors.

questions.explanation: A pessimistic explanatory style is the habit of explaining bad events as lasting, affecting everything and caused by oneself.

questions.stem: A red apple still looks red to Jin at noon, at sunset and under a kitchen lamp. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Size constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same size even when its image on the retina changes.
Shape constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same shape even when the viewing angle changes.
Apparent movement is the perception of motion when a series of still images or lights is shown in quick succession.
Correct. Color constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same color under different lighting.

questions.explanation: Color constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same color under different lighting.

questions.stem: Children with high self-esteem get better grades, but researchers cannot tell whether self-esteem raises grades or grades raise self-esteem. Which problem is this?

options.why: The third variable problem is the possibility that an unmeasured factor causes the relationship between two correlated variables.
A scatterplot is a graph in which each point shows one individual's values on two variables.
Correct. The directionality problem is the difficulty in a correlational study of knowing which variable influences the other.
The correlation coefficient is the number from −1.00 to +1.00 that shows the direction and strength of a relationship.

questions.explanation: The directionality problem is the difficulty in a correlational study of knowing which variable influences the other.

questions.stem: What is the independent variable in this study?

options.why: This was measured, not manipulated: it is the dependent variable.

options.text: The facial expression produced by holding a pen
options.why: Correct. The independent variable is the factor the researchers changed between the two conditions.
This is a procedure for forming the groups, not a variable.

options.text: The number of participants in the study
options.why: This is the sample size, not a variable the researchers changed.

questions.explanation: The independent variable is the factor the researchers changed between the two conditions.

questions.title: Article analysis: a study of problem-solving skill

parts.prompt: Identify the research method used in the study.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the method as an experiment.
rubric.example: The study is an experiment: the researchers manipulated a variable and randomly assigned the subjects to conditions.

parts.prompt: State the operational definition of problem-solving skill.

rubric.criterion: States how the variable was measured in this study.
rubric.example: Problem-solving skill was defined as the number of new puzzles out of ten that each child later solved without help.

parts.prompt: Describe the meaning of the difference between the two group averages.

rubric.criterion: Accurately describes which group scored higher or lower and what that means for the variable measured.
rubric.example: The group that received hints solved more new puzzles. On average, the value was 7.2 for the group that received hints and 4.6 for the group that practiced alone, and a p value of 0.01 means a difference this large is unlikely to be due to chance.

parts.prompt: Identify at least one ethical guideline applied by the researchers.

rubric.criterion: Identifies an ethical guideline that the summary shows was followed.
rubric.example: Informed consent and assent: parents consented and each child agreed to take part. (Also acceptable: approval by an institutional review board; the right to withdraw.)

parts.prompt: Explain the extent to which the research findings may or may not be generalizable, using specific and relevant evidence from the study.

rubric.criterion: Explains a limit (or strength) of generalizability with reference to the sample.
rubric.example: The sample was 64 five-year-old children from one city, so the findings may not apply to people of other ages, cultures or backgrounds. Because the sample was not randomly selected from a wider population, it may not be representative.

parts.prompt: Explain how at least one of the research findings supports or refutes the researchers' hypothesis.

rubric.criterion: Uses a specific finding from the study as evidence.
rubric.example: The group that received hints solved more new puzzles. (7.2 compared with 4.6).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the finding supports the hypothesis, using a psychological concept.
rubric.example: This supports the hypothesis that help from an adult affects problem-solving skill. Because subjects were randomly assigned, the difference can be attributed to help from an adult. The finding illustrates scaffolding within the zone of proximal development: temporary support lets a child master what they could not yet do alone.

questions.title: Evidence-based question: How does long-term stress affect health, and what reduces its effects?

parts.prompt: Propose a specific and defensible claim, based in psychological science, that responds to the question.

rubric.criterion: States a claim that answers the question and can be supported by the sources.
rubric.example: Long-term stress harms health, but coping strategies and social support reduce its effects.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using at least one piece of specific and relevant evidence from one of the sources. (ii) Explain how the evidence supports your claim, using a psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding learned in AP Psychology.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from one source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source A, people with more stressful life events had more colds in the same year (r = +0.33).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through the general adaptation syndrome: prolonged stress keeps the body in the resistance phase and eventually exhausts it, which suppresses the immune system and makes illness more likely.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a psychological concept in the explanation.
rubric.example: The concept must be named and applied correctly, as in the model explanation.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using an additional piece of specific and relevant evidence from a different source. (ii) Explain how this evidence supports your claim, using a different psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from a different source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source B, workers who practiced mindfulness meditation had lower cortisol levels (9.8) than workers who listened to an audiobook (13.5).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through emotion-focused coping: meditation manages the emotional and physical reaction to stress, which lowers the body's stress-hormone response.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a different psychological concept from the one used in part B.
rubric.example: The concept must differ from the one used in part B and be applied correctly.
